title: Suggestions (Console) Beta — Launch Brief (Draft)
body:
Doc status: DRAFT (internal). Owner: Chris Osei (Product Ops). Last updated: 2026-02-21.

1) What we’re launching
We are launching the Redwood Console “Suggestions” view (beta) for cost optimization automation recommendations (initially batching + caching). The view surfaces actionable recommendations with:
- Where it applies: route / model / region (+ deployment mode where relevant)
- Estimated savings: projected $/1M tokens + estimated monthly impact, with a confidence band and “basis of estimate” section
- Risk level: low / medium / high with concrete rationale bullets (latency/quality/SLO impact + reversibility)

Beta scope is read-only (no one-click apply). We are shipping behind feature flags + tenant allowlisting.

Primary goals (beta)
- Reduce time-to-value for Optimize by making backend signals understandable and usable during onboarding
- Build trust in estimated savings and risk communication (explainability > “magic number”)
- Establish telemetry contracts to measure adoption and estimated vs realized savings

Non-goals (beta)
- No “Apply” workflow, no auto-tuning, no automatic config writes to control plane
- No guarantees of savings; all numbers are estimates and should be presented as such
- Not expanding beyond batching + caching recommendation types in beta unless explicitly approved

2) Audience & stakeholders
Internal audiences
- CS/SE/TAM: use in onboarding, QBRs, and optimization walkthroughs
- Support: handle beta questions, triage “missing telemetry” and “why did savings change” issues
- Product/Eng: validate UX, estimate accuracy, risk taxonomy, and telemetry quality

External (beta customers)
- Platform engineers / ML engineers / infra engineers responsible for cost and reliability

Primary stakeholders / owners
- Product: Aditya Rao (Optimize), Marissa Cole (Console), Chris Osei (rollout coordination)
- Eng: Dylan Brooks (Console & tooling), Chloe Martin (Console backend), Logan Wright (telemetry/analytics)
- Applied ML/Evals: Jonas Weber (methodology), Karthik Iyer (validation), Selene Huang (quality guardrails)
- Design: Tessa Morgan
- Support: Dev Patel
- Security review: Naomi Feldman

3) Customer-facing positioning (internal talk track)
High-level message
“Suggestions helps you safely reduce inference cost by highlighting configuration opportunities (batching/caching) and explaining expected savings and risk. It’s a beta: numbers are estimates based on recent traffic patterns and available telemetry, and recommendations are informational only.”

Key value props to emphasize
- Actionable: tells you what to change and where, not just dashboards
- Transparent: shows basis of estimate + assumptions
- Safety-first: risk level + rationale and guardrails; designed to prevent blind changes
- Measurable: we’re instrumenting adoption and savings measurement over time

Language to avoid
- “Guaranteed savings” / “will save $X” / “safe to apply”
- Over-precision: do not quote a single number without referencing estimate uncertainty

4) What’s in the beta UI (Console)
Nav / placement
- Console → Optimize → Suggestions (beta)

List view
- Table rows = suggestion objects
- Filters: route, model, region, suggestion type (batching/caching), risk level
- Columns: suggestion summary, estimated savings (range), risk chip, last computed timestamp
- Empty states: no suggestions due to insufficient data; feature not enabled; or telemetry stale

Detail drawer
- “What to change”: proposed config adjustment(s) and affected scope
- “Why it helps”: plain language explanation of batching/caching economics
- “Estimated savings”: $/1M tokens and monthly estimate + confidence band
- “Risk”: level + rationale bullets + assumptions (e.g., latency headroom, workload variance)
- “Basis of estimate”: what telemetry windows were used, baseline period, freshness, exclusions

5) Rollout plan (internal)
Rollout principle
Small allowlisted cohort, heavy monitoring, weekly iteration. Prefer disabling over “pushing through” if estimates or tenant isolation look suspect.

Phases
Phase 0: internal dogfooding (Redwood tenants only)
- Goal: validate RBAC gating, audit logging, stale estimate detection, UX clarity

Phase 1: beta cohort (external)
- Enable per-tenant with flags; read-only
- Weekly check-ins with cohort owners (CSM/SE) + product/eng

Exit criteria (beta → broader beta)
- Savings estimate quality: acceptable error distribution (see KPI section)
- No P0 tenant isolation/security issues; audit logs validated
- Support readiness: low confusion rates; documented troubleshooting workflows
- Telemetry freshness SLO met for enabled tenants

6) Enablement steps (how to turn on for a tenant)
Prereqs
- Confirm customer is in approved beta cohort list (see cohort sheet)
- Confirm customer understands read-only beta + “estimates not guarantees” positioning
- Confirm RBAC expectations: who can view Suggestions

Enablement (prod)
1) Add tenant/workspace to allowlist (admin tool)
2) Flip feature flag: suggestions_beta = true
3) Verify permission: viewer role should NOT bypass; only authorized roles should see Suggestions
4) Verify data appears:
   - Console page loads
   - /suggestions endpoint returns tenant-scoped results
   - Risk chip + estimate fields render
5) Confirm audit logging is emitting “suggestions.read” events with correct tenant id

Verification checklist (quick)
- Open Suggestions list with a non-admin user: should not see page if lacking permission
- Switch workspace: suggestions should not bleed across workspaces
- Confirm “last computed” timestamp is recent (not stale)

Rollback
- Disable feature flag for tenant (immediate)
- Remove allowlist entry (belt-and-suspenders)
- If incident: follow SRE guidance to pause all beta enables until root cause is addressed

7) Support readiness
Support entry points
- #support escalation path: tag “Suggestions beta” and include tenant id + suggestion_id(s)
- Engineering escalation:
  - Console UI/BFF: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
  - Telemetry freshness + metering: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman
  - Risk level questions: Jonas Weber / Selene Huang

Top expected tickets & recommended responses
A) “Why did my savings estimate change week-to-week?” (SUP-19344)
- Expected in beta; estimates are computed from a rolling baseline window.
- Ask: did traffic pattern change (prompt length, concurrency, model mix), or region routing shift?
- Point to “Basis of estimate” for baseline window and freshness; if freshness is old, treat as bug.

B) “It says insufficient telemetry but we have traffic” (SUP-19361)
- Check telemetry freshness and whether traffic is on the covered routes/models.
- Validate metering pipeline ingestion for that tenant; look for dropped spans/metrics.
- If baselines older than threshold, file incident/bug; do not advise customers to act on stale numbers.

C) “High risk is too vague—what does it mean?” (SUP-19402)
- Point to rationale bullets in detail drawer; high risk generally implies low latency headroom, high variance, or low confidence in cache hit-rate/batching suitability.
- Reinforce reversibility: recommendations are informational; customers can test in staging and monitor p95 latency/quality.

Support assets to prepare before first external enable
- Support FAQ (beta) + canned replies for the three cases above
- Link to internal docs page (Console docs draft + troubleshooting)
- Internal rubric for “when to escalate to incident vs normal bug”

8) Known limitations (must be communicated internally and in docs)
Product limitations
- Read-only (no apply). Any action requires manual change by customer in their configs.
- Only batching + caching suggestions in beta.
- Recommendations may be suppressed for safety/guardrails (e.g., insufficient eval coverage or high regression risk).

Data/estimation limitations
- Estimates depend on recent telemetry quality; low traffic routes may have wide confidence bands.
- Savings may not include second-order effects (e.g., downstream retries, client-side timeouts) and may not capture all infra costs depending on deployment mode.
- Multi-suggestion interactions: we have mitigation for double-counting, but edge cases may remain.

UX limitations
- Some “no suggestions” states may be confusing; we are iterating copy.
- Confidence is currently reflected via estimate band + risk; we are evaluating whether to show an explicit confidence field.

Security/compliance limitations
- Cost/usage-derived data is sensitive; access is gated by RBAC and audited.
- Do not export or share screenshots externally without customer approval.

9) Metrics & success criteria (beta)
Adoption / usage
- % of enabled tenants with at least 1 Suggestions visit per week
- Suggestion detail open rate (from list)
- “Trust” proxy signals: time on detail, copy/tooltip interactions, repeat visits

Estimate quality
- Estimated vs realized savings (where measurable): directionally correct, and error within defined tolerance bands per workload slice
- Frequency of “insufficient telemetry” and “stale estimate” states after enablement

Reliability / safety
- No incidents due to tenant isolation regressions
- Stale estimate alerts below threshold; suggestions-service error rates within SLO

Support load
- Ticket volume per enabled tenant; primary themes and resolution time

10) Comms plan (internal)
Internal announcement
- Post in #announcements and #support on the day we enable the first external tenant
- Include: what it is, how to request enablement, known limitations, escalation paths

Customer comms
- Beta invite email template (Aditya) + optional walkthrough scheduling
- Set expectations: read-only, estimates not guarantees, we want feedback on clarity and trust

11) Weekly beta check-in agenda (30 min)
Cadence: weekly for first 4 weeks after first external enable; revisit after.

Attendees (core)
- Product: Marissa, Aditya, Chris
- Eng: Dylan (or delegate), Chloe (or delegate), Logan (or delegate)
- Support/CS: Dev, Rachel (or cohort owner), SE lead as needed
- Applied ML: Jonas or Selene (when risk/guardrails topics are on deck)

Agenda
1) Rollout status (5 min)
   - Tenants enabled this week; any enable/rollback events
2) KPI snapshot (10 min)
   - Visits, suggestions viewed, estimate freshness, “no suggestions” rates
   - Top deltas vs last week
3) Customer feedback & support tickets (10 min)
   - Top 3 themes, quotes, blockers
   - Review open Jira items (SUP-*) + responsible owner
4) Engineering updates / risks (5 min)
   - Deploys shipped, incidents, upcoming changes to schema/UX

Outputs
- Updated decision log: what we changed, why, and any cohort messaging updates
- Action items with owner + due date

12) Open questions / decisions needed
- Do we expose an explicit “confidence score” separate from risk in v1 UI, or keep folded into estimate bands + risk? (ref: #product thread 1711006621)
- Telemetry freshness gating: do we hide savings numbers if baselines older than N hours, or show with a strong “stale” warning? (ref: #eng-platform thread 1710754901)
- Criteria for adding new recommendation types during beta (and how we validate risk/quality signals)

Appendix: Requesting beta enablement (internal)
If you want to add a customer to the cohort, DM Chris Osei with:
- Tenant/workspace id
- Primary workload (chat/embeddings/rerank) + top models
- Deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- Named customer contact + internal owner (CSM/SE)
- Any compliance constraints (e.g., restricted access, need for audit trail)

Change log
- 2026-02-06: Initial draft created
- 2026-02-12: Added support readiness + top ticket responses, added weekly agenda
- 2026-02-21: Updated limitations + enablement checklist; added linked artifacts + open questions
